The **Struktureret undervisningsprogram** (structured educational program) is a clinical intervention designed to provide systematic patient education to individuals diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation). Within the Danish healthcare system's quality monitoring framework, this program is operationalized as a formal process indicator to evaluate the standard of care provided to newly diagnosed patients.

Specifically, the intervention forms the basis of [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients who receive this structured education within the first year after their diagnosis is established [^src1]. The program is part of a broader systematic set of quality indicators managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to standardize, monitor, and improve atrial fibrillation treatment across Denmark.

To ensure adequate patient education, the national quality standard for this indicator mandates that at least 50% (≥ 50%) of newly diagnosed patients must receive the structured educational program within one year of diagnosis [^src1]. This benchmark allows health authorities to evaluate whether clinical departments are successfully integrating systematic patient education into their standard care pathways for atrial fibrillation.
